chief_complaint: severe orthostatic headache that completely vanishes within minutes of lying flat
hpi_details: 41F presenting with severe positional headache when standing, neck stiffness, and MRI showing diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement, sagging brainstem, and epidural fluid collection.
ideas: She thinks her headaches are caused by severe dehydration and a strained neck muscle that pulls whenever she stands upright.
concerns: She is worried that a brain tumor is pulling downward on her brain and that she will be permanently bedridden and unable to care for her children.
expectations: She hopes to find out what is causing the pain when upright and get a treatment that allows her to stand without agony.

available_results.value: Diffuse smooth pachymeningeal enhancement, brainstem sagging, and a spinal epidural fluid collection
available_results.note: Findings support spontaneous intracranial hypotension from a CSF leak.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension (CSF Leak).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Post-lumbar puncture headache without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as progressive worsening despite lying flat, which could suggest a subdural hematoma complication.

teaching.one_liner: A leak of cerebrospinal fluid, often from a small tear in the spinal dura, causes a distinctive headache that is severe when upright but vanishes within minutes of lying flat, because the brain literally 'sags' when CSF volume drops.
red_flags: Progressive worsening despite lying flat, which could suggest a subdural hematoma complication

must_ask.say: Does the headache get much worse when you stand up, and go away when you lie flat?
How quickly does it improve once you lie down?
Have you had a spinal tap, epidural, or back surgery recently?
Any neck stiffness with the headache?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: Whenever I stand up or sit upright, I get this terrible, throbbing headache, but it completely goes away within minutes when I lie flat.
It started about five days ago as a dull ache, and over the course of a few hours, it became this intense headache that strikes every time I stand up.
It happens continuously every single day whenever I am upright. I used to get an occasional mild tension headache, but I have never felt anything like this before.
It hurts all over the back of my head and neck, and then spreads forward to both temples.
It feels like a heavy, pulling, throbbing pressure. When I am standing on my feet, it reaches about an 8 out of 10 in severity.
The headache stays the entire time I am upright and gets heavier through the day, but after a night of sleeping flat in bed, I wake up completely free of pain.
Standing up, walking around, and coughing make it unbearable, but lying down completely flat relieves it completely.
Once my head is completely flat on a pillow, the pain starts fading within two or three minutes and is totally gone within ten minutes.
No, I have not had any flashing lights, blind spots, zigzag patterns, or tingling sensations before it starts.
I get a bit nauseated and sensitive to bright lights when the headache is severe, but I have not thrown up.
No, my eyes do not tear up or get red, and I do not have a runny or stuffy nose.
I have not had any fever, chills, or skin rashes at all.
Yes, the back of my neck feels very stiff and tight whenever I am upright, but it loosens up as soon as I lie down flat.
No, I do not have any weakness in my arms or legs, and no numbness or tingling anywhere.
No, my speech has been totally clear, and I have not had any confusion or seizures.
My vision gets slightly blurry and my ears feel muffled or full when I stand, but I do not have double vision or hearing loss.
No, I have not bumped my head, fallen, or had any physical trauma recently.
I tried taking ibuprofen and acetaminophen a couple of times each day, but neither of them helped while I was standing.
There are no triggers like stress, certain foods, or missed sleep; the only trigger is sitting up or standing on my feet.
No, I have never had a spinal tap, an epidural injection, or any kind of back or neck surgery in my life.
This positional headache has been going on continuously for the past five days.
I have high blood pressure and take a blood pressure pill every morning, but I do not take aspirin or any blood thinners.
No one else at home has a headache, and our home heating is modern and working properly.
No, I have never had cancer, and I have no immune problems or immune-suppressing medications.
I thought I was just severely dehydrated and had a strained neck muscle pulling on my head whenever I stand up.
I'm worried sick that there is a tumor in my brain and that I won't be able to get out of bed to raise my kids.
I want an answer as to why this only hits me when I stand up, and some treatment so I can be on my feet again today.
I was diagnosed with high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol a few years ago.
I have never had any surgeries, and I have never stayed overnight in a hospital.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day every morning, plus an over-the-counter daily multivitamin.
No, I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used any nicotine products.
I drink socially on occasion, maybe one glass of wine a couple of times a month, but I have not had any alcohol since this started.
I work as an accountant and live with my husband and teenage daughter in an apartment.
My mother has high blood pressure, but no one in my family has had brain aneurysms, migraines, or any neurological disorders.
My last menstrual period started two weeks ago and my cycles are normal and regular. My husband had a vasectomy, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 126/80 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respirations 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Alert and comfortable while lying flat on the examination table, but displays noticeable distress and grimacing when asked to sit up.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light, extraocular movements are full without nystagmus, and fundoscopy demonstrates sharp optic disc margins without papilledema.
No tenderness on palpation of the frontal or maxillary sinuses, and temporal arteries are soft, non-tender, and pulseless without bruits.
Mild resistance and pain on passive terminal neck flexion, with negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
Mild tenderness and spasm in the posterior cervical paraspinal muscles without focal midline cervical or thoracic spine bony tenderness.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial sensation, normal palate elevation, and symmetric shoulder shrug.
Normal muscle bulk and tone, with 5/5 motor strength in all major muscle groups of the bilateral upper and lower extremities.
Intact light touch, pinprick, and vibration sensation symmetrically throughout all dermatomes.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric at the biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles tendons; plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing are intact without dysmetria, and gait is steady without ataxia, though standing promptly reproduces her severe headache.
